title: SUMO issue #7615 — inconsistent OSM typemap
relevance: The issue reports that highway=path permits pedestrians and bicycles but defaults to oneWay, creating an unrealistic bicycle-network constraint in the reported context.
boundary: Closed issue opened in 2020 and updated in 2025; it documents a specific reported mapping inconsistency, not proof that the same bug persists in current releases or that the issue is an independent reproduction.
next_action: Use as a negative test pattern: type mapping must validate cross-field semantic consistency and preserve source/override provenance.

title: SUMO issue #7119 — reconsider default permissions on roads for pedestrians
relevance: The report describes how default pedestrian permissions on road lanes and alternative typemaps for separately mapped sidewalks can surprise users and affect network semantics.
boundary: Closed issue opened in 2020 and updated in 2025; historical project discussion, not a current compliance rule or independent field validation.
next_action: Use as a negative test pattern: access modes and physical sidewalk edges must not be silently inferred from a single road-type label.

title: SUMO issue #15013 — undone join operations appear in junction join output
relevance: The issue reports that the junction join output can include intermediate join states, including operations later undone in the editor.
boundary: Open issue last updated 2026-10-09; concerns an audit/output artifact, not proof that the final network geometry itself is wrong.
next_action: Use as a traceability test pattern: final geometry state, proposed edits, undo history and exported audit logs must be distinguished.
